A wide panoramic illustration of the solar system. On the far left is a massive glowing Sun. Sweeping out to the right are the elliptical orbits of the planets. Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are shown close to the Sun. A ring of irregular rocky asteroids (the Asteroid Belt) separates them from the giant planets: Jupiter (with its Great Red Spot), Saturn (with wide bright rings), Uranus, and Neptune. Far to the right is the tiny icy body of Pluto. A comet with a glowing tail sweeping away from the Sun is shown in the background. Clean flat textbook style, dark space background with white orbit lines and accurate planet colours.

A diagram showing the Earth and the Moon in space. A large, blue and green Earth is in the centre, with the grey, cratered Moon orbiting it along a white dashed circular path. Double-headed arrows show the gravitational pull of the Moon acting on the Earth's oceans, creating a visible bulge of blue water facing the Moon (high tide).

A three-part vertical cross-section diagram of the Earth's surface showing the three segments. The top section shows a light blue sky with clouds representing the Atmosphere, accompanied by a small pie chart showing $78\%$ $\text{N}_2$ and $21\%$ $\text{O}_2$. The middle section shows a deep blue ocean layer representing the Hydrosphere, with the chemical formula $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ + $\text{NaCl}$. The bottom section shows a cross-section of brown, rocky land representing the Lithosphere, accompanied by a small pie chart showing $47\%$ Oxygen and $28\%$ Silicon.
